messages:
lucy: quick q — we're sketching a change to collector topology. want to enforce tenant quotas and routing priority without blowing up gateway tails when N small tenants spike. do we: (A) keep agent-local per-signal pipelines + lightweight gateway router only for egress, or (B) centralize per-signal pipelines in gateway and do tenant sharding there? tradeoffs?

mike: +1 to bringing this up. my gut: agents should keep signal separation for latency-sensitive spans, but gateway needs smarter backpressure. main problem is gateway CPU+exporter saturation during fan-in.

sara: agree w/ mike. also concerned about retention/enrichment order if we move pipelines to gateway — we might lose useful local sampling decisions.

jordan: what if we do hybrid: agent does initial per-signal lightweight pipeline (sampling + kv attach) and gateway hosts the heavier exporters + tenant quota enforcement & prioritization? gateway can then elect to shed lower-priority tenants early.

lucy: that hybrid sounds plausible. two open questions: 1) how do we communicate tenant-priority/weight to gateway efficiently? 2) where to store per-tenant retention policies so gateway can drop or route correctly?

mike: for 1) attach a compact header in the OTLP envelope from agent -> gateway: e.g., "x-rd-tenant-score: 0.1". gateway uses that for a fast token-bucket selector. avoid full policy eval in hot path.

sara: for 2) store retention/policy in gateway's in-memory config that syncs from control-plane on change. control-plane pushes diffs. default fallback if missing = global policy. keep policy lookup O(1).

jordan: +1. also add a periodic bloom-filter style cache for tenant bloom -> known heavy exporters so we can avoid per-tenant DB hits.

infra-bot: deploy-check: can we add a canary to 10% of hosts to validate policy sync latency? suggested rollout config: 10% -> 30% -> 100% with auto-rollback on exporter error rate > 1% in 5m.

lucy: thinking through backpressure: gateway should expose two shedding knobs — coarse tenant-slice (shard-level) and fine priority score. if a shard > threshold, gateway sheds all low-priority tenants in that shard. implement with per-shard token buckets + per-tenant decrement.

mike: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
# gateway incoming path
tenant_shard = shard(tenant_id)
if shard_token_bucket.consume(1) == false:
  if tenant_priority < SHED_THRESHOLD:
    drop(span)
  else:
    try_queue_for_retry(span)
```
Works for us?

sara: looks ok. question: do we count spans equally? some spans are huge (lots of attributes) — maybe we should charge by approximate byte-size. cheaper to track token usage by token_count ~ estimate_bytes/256.

jordan: yep, use cost model. also record metrics per-shard: dropped_spans_total{shard=..,reason=priority}. that'll help runtime ops.

lucy: ops/observability: we need dashboard that shows shard-level token utilization and top shed tenants. add alert if >5% of incoming span volume is being shed for >2m.

mike: quick note on exporter saturation: configure exporter_pool_size per-shard and let gateway route to fallback region/model in cases of sustained exporter queueing. fallback should preserve priority order.

sara: retention enforcement: when gateway drops spans due to retention, it should emit an audit event with tenant_id + retention_policy_version so downstream billing/cc teams can reconcile.

jordan: one more: agent firewall rules — if agent can't reach gateway for policy sync, it should continue with cached local policies and start exponential backoff. don't flip to default global policy unless cache age > X (configurable).

lucy: sounds like action items: 1) prototype gateway shard token-bucket + per-tenant score header (mike) 2) control-plane policy diff protocol + in-memory sync (sara) 3) telemetry dashboards & alerts (jordan) 4) rollout canary + infra-bot config (lucy)

mike: i'll spike the token-bucket prototype today, will share a small bench (qps vs drop-rate).

sara: i'll draft the policy diff schema and fallback semantics.

jordan: i'll make dashboard wireframes and metric names.

lucy: awesome. tagging @mike @sara @jordan for follow-ups. thanks :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket created: RD-TELEMETRY-3872 "gateway shard quotas + tenant-priority proto" assigned to mike/sara/jordan, due 2025-01-08.
